harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-04T14:57:07.185000+00:00

attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-04T14:57:07.185000+00:00

diagnosis.summary: Executor eventually got a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster running with AMQP-TLS on 5671 and management restricted to the cluster subnet, but spent a large share of the session fighting package-repo/signing-key fetch failures, then a rabbitmqctl-observed queue-unresponsiveness problem surfaced right after a self-triggered node1 reboot, and the cluster lease expired (14:57:07) while that was still being investigated — so final validated state (e.g. a CA-issued client actually connecting, and the queue fully recovering) is not confirmed in the evidence.

evidence.finding: rabbitmq-server and erlang were not pre-installed; executor had to install from scratch on all 3 nodes.

evidence.source: node1/node2/node3 curl to raw.githubusercontent.com signing keys, 14:37:52-14:38:06
evidence.finding: epel-release installed fine, but the combined command returned exit code 1 and a follow-up ls found no rabbit/cloudsmith key files — the signing-key curls failed silently.

evidence.source: cloudsmith setup.rpm.sh curl+bash on all 3 nodes, 14:38:19-14:38:21
evidence.finding: return_code 22 (curl -f HTTP error) on all three nodes — the Cloudsmith bootstrap script URL was unreachable or erroring.

evidence.source: node1 custom repo file + rpm --import + dnf install, 14:41:45
evidence.finding: Command failed with a 120-second proxy read timeout (AntriebMCPError), i.e. the install ran long enough to exceed the exec proxy limit; the redacted base64 blob content is unknown.
Despite the earlier timeout error, rabbitmq-server was later found 'active', implying the install (or a retry) succeeded in the background after the timed-out exec call.

TLS handshake failure logged: {tls_alert,{bad_certificate,...,"selfsigned_peer"}} for a peer at 10.100.149.10:44550 — consistent with the cluster correctly rejecting a client cert not issued by the configured CA.

Port 5671/tcp open publicly (matches AMQP-TLS client access requirement); rich rules restrict 25672, 15672, 4369 to source 10.100.149.0/24 only (matches 'management reachable only within cluster' requirement). No --permanent flag evidence, so persistence across reboot is unconfirmed.

evidence.source: node2 curl to node1:15672 via ssh, 14:51:31
evidence.finding: 200 OK from within the cluster subnet, confirming management UI is reachable from cluster peers as intended.

evidence.source: node1 boot_id/uptime before and after reboot, 14:51:40-14:52:14
evidence.finding: Executor deliberately rebooted node1 (systemctl reboot); node came back up within ~30s and rejoined the cluster (rabbit@node1/node2/node3 all listed as Running Nodes at 14:52:18).
Both calls hit RabbitMQ's own internal 60-second timeout with 'Some queue(s) are unresponsive' for tls_test_q, despite the queue separately being reported as state=running.
This call itself hit the platform's 120-second proxy timeout — the unresponsiveness investigation was still unresolved when time ran out.
Cluster lease expired at 14:57:07, shortly after the last (still-timing-out) diagnostic command at 14:56:39.

likely_causes.cause: RabbitMQ/Erlang signing-key and repo-setup URLs (raw.githubusercontent.com paths, Cloudsmith setup.rpm.sh) were stale, wrong, or unreachable from this environment, forcing a manual/undocumented repo-file workaround that itself then exceeded the exec proxy timeout.

The dnf install of erlang+rabbitmq-server legitimately took longer than 120 seconds (likely due to EPEL/Cloudsmith dependency resolution or slow mirrors) and was run as a single blocking exec instead of the platform's recommended background+poll pattern, causing a false 'failed' result even though the install ultimately succeeded.

A classic (non-quorum) test queue (tls_test_q) became unresponsive after node1 was rebooted mid-session — likely a general RabbitMQ classic-queue/Mnesia resync characteristic on restart rather than a TLS-specific issue — and repeated rabbitmqctl polling against it consumed the remaining time budget until the lease expired before recovery could be confirmed.

The observed bad_certificate/selfsigned_peer TLS alert is very likely an intentional negative test (client presenting a non-CA cert being correctly rejected) rather than a misconfiguration, but the evidence does not include a matching positive test showing a CA-issued client cert succeeding, so mTLS enforcement is only half-verified.

next_attempt_guidance: Before attempting package installation, verify outbound reachability to the RabbitMQ/Erlang key and repo hosts (raw.githubusercontent.com, dl.cloudsmith.io, github.com release assets) with a plain curl -I/-v probe on one node first, rather than looping through multiple bootstrap methods live.

Run `dnf install -y erlang rabbitmq-server` using the primer's background+poll pattern (`cmd > /tmp/out.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/pid`, then `tail` in follow-up execs) instead of a single blocking exec, to avoid false failures from the 120-second proxy timeout.

After installing, explicitly verify TLS mutual-auth from both directions: attempt one client connection using a certificate signed by the cluster CA (expect success) and one with a cert not signed by that CA or no cert (expect rejection) — capture both outcomes rather than relying on an incidental log line.

For any test queues, prefer quorum queues (not classic) if the plan includes rebooting a node, since classic queues on a single node showed post-reboot unresponsiveness in this attempt; if classic queues are required by the task, confirm they recover fully (rabbitmqctl list_queues returns promptly) before moving on, and budget extra time for that check.

Confirm firewalld rules for the management port (15672) and inter-node ports are applied with --permanent (or otherwise persisted) so they survive a reboot, and re-check firewall-cmd --list-all after any reboot.

Track elapsed time against the lease window explicitly — this attempt spent roughly the first 5 minutes on repo/signing-key troubleshooting and the last several minutes stuck on queue-unresponsiveness diagnostics with no successful conclusion before expiry; leave a time buffer to finish validation and produce a final status report before the lease is likely to end.
